metadata.name: limit_order
metadata.description: Non-custodial limit orders on Cookie Chain, filled by flash-fill sandwich

accounts.name: keeper
docs: Anyone. Garbage collection is permissionless so the keeper can reap expired orders;
the funds and the rent still go to the maker, so there is nothing to gain by it
beyond paying the transaction fee.

accounts.name: maker_input_account
docs: Checked against the account pinned at placement, not merely against the mint — a
cancel cannot be redirected any more than a fill can. Either a token account for
`input_mint`, or the maker's wallet for a native-refund order (see `initialize_order`).

accounts.name: maker_input_account
docs: GUARD 6 — anti-griefing. Anyone can donate input tokens straight into the reserve, and a
token account cannot be closed while it holds a balance, so without a sweep a one-unit
donation would make the final fill of an order revert forever. Whatever the reserve still
holds after the fill is returned to the account pinned at placement.

accounts.name: maker_output_account
docs: GUARD 4 — pinned at placement. The maker's price is paid *here*, never to an account
the taker chooses. Either a token account for `output_mint` (the token program rejects a
mint mismatch on transfer) or, for a native-output order, the maker's wallet itself.

accounts.name: payout
docs: Scratch account for a native payout: created, filled with the maker's wCOOK, closed for
its lamports and released again, all inside this instruction. Unused (and untouched) for
a token-account payout, but always passed so there is one instruction, one account list.

accounts.name: taker_input_account
docs: The taker pays the maker out of this account — the proceeds of whatever swap it did.

accounts.name: input_mint
docs: Needed only to sweep and close the reserve once the order is fully filled.

accounts.name: maker_input_account
docs: GUARD 6 — whatever was donated into the reserve goes back to the account pinned at
placement, so a dust donation cannot make the last fill revert forever.

accounts.name: user_position
docs: GUARD 4 — pinned at placement: the maker's own position on the pinned pool. This is where
the price must have been paid, and it is the only account this fill will count.

accounts.name: taker_fee_source
docs: The taker's fee is charged in the INPUT mint — a share cannot be transferred.

accounts.name: admin
docs: Checked in the handler with `assert_admin`, deliberately NOT with `address = ADMIN`.
Anchor writes an `address` constraint into the IDL as the account's address, so the
constraint form publishes whichever key the build compiled in — and a `--features local`
build would publish the test admin, whose secret is in `tests/helpers/index.ts`. The IDL
then differs between builds for no good reason (see the README). Same gate, same error,
no key in the artifact.

accounts.name: base
docs: A throwaway keypair supplied by the client. It seeds the order PDA, so a maker can
have unlimited concurrent orders with no nonce counter to race on.

accounts.name: reserve
docs: The escrow vault, owned by the order PDA.

accounts.name: maker_input_account
docs: The account the escrow is funded FROM. It is also pinned as the refund destination —
unless `refund_native` is set (native input only), in which case the maker's wallet is
pinned instead and a cancel/expiry closes the reserve straight into it as lamports. A
maker who paid COOK then gets COOK back, with no wCOOK left to unwrap by hand.

accounts.name: maker_output_account
docs: Pinned onto the order — every fill pays here and nowhere else. Either a token account
for `output_mint` (its owner is *not* constrained to the maker: a maker may want the
output delivered to another account they control), or — only when `output_mint` is the
native mint — the maker's own wallet, in which case a fill pays lamports, not wCOOK.
Validated in `assert_output_destination`.

accounts.name: curve_pool
docs: CURVE BUY only: the MomoSwap pool whose curve this order buys on. Validated in
`assert_curve_destination` and pinned onto the order. `None` for every other kind.
Kept LAST so the account indices of everything above are unchanged: a client built
against the previous IDL that omits it still places non-curve orders (Anchor reads a
missing trailing optional account as `None`).

accounts.name: taker_output_account
docs: The taker receives the order's *input* token here — the leg it will swap. Passing the
reserve itself would be a self-transfer no-op that still flips `waiting`; refuse it.

accounts.name: instructions
docs: `flash_fill_order` appears later in this same transaction.

instructions.name: pre_flash_fill_order_curve
docs: Curve BUY fills — the shares-delta path. See `instructions/curve_fill.rs`.

accounts.name: taker_output_account
docs: The taker receives the maker's escrowed COOK here — what it pays the curve with.

accounts.name: user_position
docs: The maker's launchpad position, pinned at placement. Read-only here: all this
instruction does with it is write down what it held before the buy.

accounts.name: admin
docs: Checked in the handler — see `InitFee::admin`.

accounts.name: admin
docs: Checked in the handler — see `InitFee::admin`.

types.name: Fee
docs: Global fee configuration — a singleton at `["fee"]` that is *also* the token authority
over every `program_fee_account`.
The fee deliberately does not live on the `Order`: keeping it here means it is
retunable by the admin with no program upgrade and no account migration.

fields.name: maker_fee
docs: Deducted from what the maker receives on a fill (Jupiter's platform fee): the maker is
paid `required_out - maker_fee`, the vault gets the difference. This is the fee that is
real revenue whoever fills — a taker fee paid by our own keeper is pocket to pocket.

fields.name: taker_fee
docs: Charged to the taker on top of the maker's limit price.

types.name: Order
docs: A resting limit order. Field names match Jupiter Limit Order v2 so its published IDL
stays a usable reference.
"Making" is the maker's side: the input token it escrows. "Taking" is what the maker
requires back. A fill is `pre_flash_fill_order` (release input to the taker) followed,
in the same transaction, by `flash_fill_order` (pull the required output back out of
the taker).

fields.name: waiting
docs: A fill is mid-flight: input has been released but not yet settled. The reentrancy
guard — two releases against one settlement would double-spend the reserve.

fields.name: making_amount
docs: Input still escrowed in the reserve.

fields.name: taking_amount
docs: Output still required for the remaining `making_amount`.

fields.name: maker_input_account
docs: PINNED at placement — a cancel refunds only here.

fields.name: maker_output_account
docs: PINNED at placement — a fill pays only here.

fields.name: borrow_making_amount
docs: Set by `pre_flash_fill_order`, consumed by `flash_fill_order`.

fields.name: expired_at
docs: `None` = good-til-cancelled.

fields.name: base
docs: The PDA seed. A throwaway keypair the client generates and signs with, rather than a
nonce counter — no read-then-write race when two placements are in flight.

fields.name: kind
docs: `ORDER_KIND_LIMIT` or `ORDER_KIND_STOP`. A stop is a below-market trigger: the program
still guarantees the maker at least `taking_amount` (the FLOOR), but only `STOP_KEEPER`
may fill it, and that keeper waits for the market to fall to `trigger_taking_amount`.

fields.name: created_at
docs: Unix time the order was placed, for ordering in clients. Informational only.

fields.name: trigger_taking_amount
docs: STOP only: the output (for `ori_making_amount`) at which the stop ARMS — stop-market
semantics. Once the market pays this or less, the keeper sells at whatever the market
gives, down to the floor `taking_amount`. Placed as `>= ori_taking_amount`. Informational
to the program (only the keeper reads it); the floor is what the program enforces.
0 for a plain limit order.

fields.name: curve_pool
docs: CURVE BUY only: the MomoSwap pool pinned at placement. It binds `maker_output_account` to
`["user", pool, maker]` and it is what a fill re-derives the position from, so a taker
cannot point the settlement at a position on some other pool. `default()` otherwise.

fields.name: curve_shares_before
docs: CURVE BUY only: `UserPosition.shares` as it stood when `pre_flash_fill_order_curve`
released the input. The settlement compares against this, because the program cannot move
shares itself — they are non-transferable and live inside the launchpad's account.
